vision: Experiment #19b (rewrite): build an investigative AI agent that examines real code commits — gathering diff, message, and repository evidence — and produces structured risk assessments with explanations. ApacheJIT is the test bed not because we need another classifier, but because its replication package provides a rare 5-dimensional validation chain (bug-inducing commit → fixing commit → JIRA issue) covering 100% of 28K positives. The deliverable is a solid, verifiable investigation harness that proves harness engineering (context construction, routing, verification, cost governance) matters more than raw model quality — with optional XGBoost routing demonstrating when to skip, flag, or investigate.
direction: Complete rewrite: delete the ITSM 9-stage pipeline (`src/cr_analyzer/`, `tests/`, `fixtures/`, pipeline docs). Keep `data/apachejit/`, `scripts/download_apachejit.sh`, `.harness/` structure, git history. New Python package (name TBD in scaffold task) with framework-agnostic interfaces: GroundTruthGraph, GitContextProvider, InvestigationReport schema, AgentOrchestrator (bounded multi-turn loop), ToolRegistry, XGBoostRouter, and FiveDimensionEvalHarness. V1 uses local git clones of 2 Apache projects (Camel + Hadoop), real diffs/messages, LLM reasoning inside a deterministic orchestrator. Ground truth richness is first-class: load commit_links + JIRA linkage from replication package; JIRA API for eval dimensions 3–5 only. Cost governance: XGBoost scores all commits free; LLM investigates only routed gray-zone samples within budget tiers. Framework choice (LangGraph vs minimal) deferred to post-V1 spike.

cleanup.rationale: Prior codebase was an ITSM batch pipeline forced onto ApacheJIT via adapter — wrong abstraction for commit investigation. Ground truth discovery (commit_links + JIRA chain) justifies a purpose-built investigative agent. Pipeline code is archived in git history and .harness/archive/, not evolved.

trade_offs.decision: Investigative agent, not classifier — primary output is structured investigation report with evidence and reasoning
trade_offs.alternative: XGBoost/ML classifier on numeric features only
trade_offs.reasoning: ApacheJIT's rich ground truth enables 5-dimension validation (prediction, localization, diagnosis, severity, recommendations) that no classifier output supports. ML router is a harness component, not the product.

trade_offs.decision: Bounded multi-turn agent loop (max 3 turns V1) with explicit follow-up triggers
trade_offs.alternative: Single-pass (gather → reason → output) or unbounded ReAct
trade_offs.reasoning: Investigation requires following evidence (e.g., file history after seeing risky diff), but unbounded loops are unbounded cost. V1: turn 1 = diff+message+features+initial scan; turns 2–3 = targeted dig (file history, author stats) only when confidence < threshold or explicit uncertainty flagged.

trade_offs.decision: Orchestrator + LLM reasoning steps — LLM is not the entire system
trade_offs.alternative: End-to-end LLM agent with no deterministic layer
trade_offs.reasoning: Harness thesis requires deterministic context construction, budget gates, schema validation, routing, and checkpointing around LLM calls. Orchestrator owns tool dispatch, turn limits, and report assembly; LLM owns reasoning over assembled context.

trade_offs.decision: V1 git access: local clones of 2 projects (Camel, Hadoop) via git CLI
trade_offs.alternative: Clone all 15 repos upfront; GitHub API on-demand for all diffs
trade_offs.reasoning: Camel has ~14K commits (largest); Hadoop provides second-project generalization. Local git enables blame/log/diff without API rate limits. All-15-repo clone is multi-GB and blocks V1; GitHub API alone cannot do blame/log efficiently. Expand to more projects in V2.

trade_offs.decision: V1 context bundle: unified diff + commit message + CSV numeric features + last-3 file commits + precomputed author project stats
trade_offs.alternative: Diff+message only (too thin); full blame + live JIRA + all file history (too expensive)
trade_offs.reasoning: LLM needs more than metrics but less than exhaustive archaeology. Numeric features ground the agent in ApacheJIT's signal without replacing investigation. Author stats precomputed from train split (no leakage). JIRA fetched at eval time, not investigation time — prevents oracle leakage during agent runs.

trade_offs.decision: XGBoost router: P<0.3 SAFE (skip LLM), P>0.7 HIGH (flag, optional light LLM confirm), 0.3≤P≤0.7 INVESTIGATE (full agent)
trade_offs.reasoning: Proves harness routing thesis at scale. 106K commits × LLM is infeasible. Router trained on train split numeric features only (fair baseline). Agent eval focuses on gray zone where investigation adds value.

trade_offs.decision: Default eval budget tier: $50 (~300 LLM investigations at ~$0.15/commit)
trade_offs.reasoning: $10 sufficient for CI smoke. $50 balances statistical power on gray-zone buggy/clean mix with cost discipline. $100 for manual deep runs. Budget is a harness governance knob, not an afterthought.

trade_offs.decision: Framework-agnostic AgentRunner protocol; LangGraph/CrewAI decision deferred
trade_offs.reasoning: User explicitly deferred framework. V1 builds against interfaces (AgentRunner, Tool, CheckpointStore). Spike after working V1 compares LangGraph vs 100-line custom loop on same tools.

trade_offs.decision: Five-dimension eval with tiered automation: D1-D2 deterministic; D3-D5 LLM-as-judge with rubric + human audit sample
trade_offs.reasoning: D1 (prediction vs buggy label) and D2 (localization vs fix diff files) are automatable. D3–D5 (diagnosis, severity, recommendations vs JIRA) need semantic judgment — LLM-as-judge scales with documented rubric; 20-commit human audit catches judge drift.

trade_offs.decision: No JIRA/oracle data in agent investigation context — reserved for eval comparison only
trade_offs.alternative: Give agent the fix commit and JIRA issue during investigation
trade_offs.reasoning: Would trivialize the task and invalidate claims about investigative capability. Agent sees what a reviewer would see at commit time; eval compares output to oracle after the fact.

open_questions: Package name: `commit_investigator`, `jit_agent`, or keep repo name aligned? Builder decides in scaffold task.
Replication package layout: exact paths for commit_links_{PROJECT}.csv and {PROJECT}.csv inside zip — feat-2 must verify user's 100% chain claim on real extracted files.
Localization GT granularity: file-level from fix diff vs line-level via GumTree mappings in replication package — line-level is higher value but may be a V2 eval dimension.
LLM provider/model for V1: need API key strategy and model lock for reproducibility (temperature=0, pinned model ID).
Diagnosis eval (D3): embed JIRA description vs agent reasoning — semantic similarity threshold or structured rubric checklist?
Severity mapping: JIRA priority/severity enums vary by project — need normalization table before D4 scoring.
Camel+Hadoop sufficient for V1 claims, or must include a third project before any generalization statement?
When to train XGBoost: after agent V1 works standalone, or parallel? Current plan: feat-6 after feat-5 so agent is independently demonstrable.
Human audit protocol for D3–D5: who reviews the 20-commit sample and where are rubrics documented?

Hard turn cap (3), per-commit token budget, per-run dollar cap enforced by orchestrator; breadcrumb cost telemetry

architectural_decisions.agent_loop: Bounded multi-turn (max 3 turns V1). Orchestrator decides follow-up vs finalize.
architectural_decisions.llm_role: Reasoning engine inside orchestrator — not the outer control plane.
architectural_decisions.git_access: Local clones, 2 projects V1 (Camel, Hadoop). git CLI for diff/log/blame.
architectural_decisions.routing: XGBoost on numeric features. Thresholds 0.3/0.7. Implemented after standalone agent.
architectural_decisions.scale_cost: Tiered budgets: $10/50/100. LLM only on routed samples. XGBoost scores full splits free.
architectural_decisions.context_per_commit: Diff + message + CSV features + file history (3) + author stats (precomputed).
architectural_decisions.ground_truth: First-class GroundTruthGraph: bug_hash → fix_hash → issue_key → JIRA metadata. Eval-only oracle access.
deferred: Framework selection (LangGraph vs minimal vs CrewAI)

tasks.name: Investigation report schema
tasks.scope: Pydantic models: EvidenceItem (type, source, content, relevance), LocalizationClaim (file, lines, rationale), Recommendation (action, priority, rationale), RiskAssessment (level: LOW|MEDIUM|HIGH|CRITICAL, confidence 0-1), CommitInvestigationReport (commit_id, project, risk_assessment, evidence[], findings[], localization[], reasoning_summary, recommendations[], tools_used[], turn_count, metadata). JSON schema export. Validation rejects reports with zero evidence items.

tasks.name: Agent investigation loop V1
tasks.scope: Framework-agnostic AgentOrchestrator: ToolRegistry (git tools, feature lookup), bounded multi-turn loop (max 3), LLM reasoning step (pluggable provider), budget tracking (tokens + estimated cost), checkpoint persistence per turn. CLI: investigate --commit <id> --project <name>. Output: CommitInvestigationReport JSON. No routing yet — every invocation runs full investigation.

tasks.name: XGBoost routing layer
tasks.scope: Train XGBoost on apachejit_train.csv numeric features (LA, LD, NF, ND, NS, ENT, NDEV, AGE, EXP, REXP, SEXP, etc.). Router classifies: SAFE (<0.3), INVESTIGATE (0.3-0.7), HIGH (>0.7). CLI: route --split test_small|test_large emits routing manifest. Integrate with orchestrator: INVESTIGATE/HIGH run agent; SAFE skips. Persist router model + metrics (AUC, calibration) for harness comparison.

tasks.name: Five-dimension evaluation harness
tasks.scope: EvalHarness sampling strategy: stratified sample from routed commits within budget tier (default $50/300 LLM calls). Score D1 prediction (risk level vs buggy label), D2 localization (agent files vs fix diff files, Jaccard + optional line overlap), D3 diagnosis (agent reasoning vs JIRA description, LLM-as-judge rubric), D4 severity calibration (agent risk vs JIRA priority, normalized mapping), D5 recommendation relevance (agent rec vs actual fix pattern, LLM-as-judge). Emit eval-report.json + eval-report.md. Include router-only baseline (no LLM) for comparison.
